$comment: Public canonical vocabulary and alias table (docs/04-benchmark-contract.md §4, rule 4). Reference material for agents and for anyone extending matching. The evaluator's normalizer (src/normalize.mjs) does NOT look values up in this file at match time for scalar semantic_facts values -- it applies structural, declared rules only (trim, path-shape, prefix casing) and never fuzzy/synonym matching. 'aliases' below is the single place where an explicit synonym could be declared for a specific (kind, subject) pair; it is EMPTY by design (ADR-14 closed the author-notation gap by restructuring values instead of aliasing them). Adding an alias here is a benchmark-authoring decision recorded in docs/11, not something the evaluator invents on its own.

order_status_labels.$comment: UI labels for semantic_facts kind=enum_mapping subject=order.statusId, drawn from apps/web/src/orderStatus.ts. The scored value is the numeric statusId; these labels live in the fact's free-text 'meaning' and are informational only -- they are never part of a matching key.

dependency_field_prefixes.$comment: docs/04 §4 rule 6. header: and cookie: names are case-folded for comparison because HTTP header names and this benchmark's single cookie name are case-insensitive on the wire; $. (JSONPath into a body) and {param} (path placeholder) are left case-sensitive because JSON keys are.
JSONPath into a response/request body, case-sensitive
dependency_field_prefixes.{param}: path placeholder, case-sensitive, drawn from the operation's own normalized path

path_placeholders.$comment: docs/04 §1: the only placeholder names ground truth uses. Not a closed enum the schema enforces -- an agent-chosen placeholder name that differs from these will simply fail to match a ground-truth operation/dependency/workflow-step key, which is a real (if maybe unfair) scoring outcome, not a bug. See evaluator/README.md 'Known interpretation calls'.

unordered_value_keys.$comment: Keys inside a structured semantic_facts.value object (definitions.semanticFactValue) whose array is treated as a set, not a sequence, when computing the canonical matching key -- ground truth writes them in one order (e.g. ascending numeric) but that order carries no semantic meaning. Declared here, applied by src/normalize.mjs normalizeValue(), so it is a public rule rather than a silent code behavior.

aliases.$comment: Explicit (kind, subject, value) synonyms the evaluator should treat as equal. Empty on purpose -- see top-level $comment. Shape if ever populated: [{"kind":"...","subject":"...","from":"...","to":"..."}]
